_note: Suggested simple lines for the MDMA batch-2 claims (AI reader 38, adjudication, 2026-10-17), written from each claim's plain and precise text as claims_patch.json and new_claims.json leave it (not yet applied). Each entry: 'short' (the answer, everyday words), 'but' (its main limit), 'how' (two to four How-we-know points) and 'v' (the claim version each entry was written from). They say no more than the claim and use 'dummy pill', not 'placebo'. For the senior author's review; WRITING-RULES requires the simple.json entry to be rewritten in the same commit as the claim.

cl_mdma_ptsd_efficacy.short: With the same therapy, PTSD scores fell more with MDMA than with a dummy pill.
cl_mdma_ptsd_efficacy.but: In the trial that asked, most people knew which pill they had.
how: In two trials run for one sponsor, 194 adults with PTSD had up to three long sessions with MDMA or a dummy pill, plus the same therapy.
About 4 months later, PTSD scores had dropped about 9 to 12 points more with MDMA, on a scale of 0 to 80.
Of those who finished, about 7 in 10 on MDMA no longer had PTSD, against 3 to 5 in 10 on the dummy pill.
Neither trial reports measuring what people expected. The trials report nothing after 4 months, and none we read compared MDMA with standard talking therapy.

cl_mdma_ptsd_blinding.short: In the trial that asked, most people could tell MDMA from the dummy pill.
cl_mdma_ptsd_blinding.but: Only one of the two trials asked, and only at the very end.
how: At the end of the second trial, 94 in 100 people on MDMA and 75 in 100 on the dummy pill guessed right.
Most said they could tell from what they felt, or did not feel. The first trial did not ask.
The people who scored PTSD did not know who had what, but the scores came from what people told them.
Neither trial reports measuring what people expected, so we cannot tell how much of the gain came from MDMA itself.

cl_mdma_ptsd_adverse_events.short: MDMA often gave brief side effects, like tight muscles, feeling sick and sweating.
cl_mdma_ptsd_adverse_events.but: The trials were too small and short to show rare or later harms.
how: In two trials, 99 people took MDMA and 95 took a dummy pill, in a clinic, with therapy.
Tight muscles affected about 59 to 61 in 100 people on MDMA, against 14 to 26 in 100 on the dummy pill.
No serious side effects were seen on MDMA; 2 people on the dummy pill had one.
The first trial did not ask about expected effects, like feeling very happy, as side effects.

cl_mdma_regulatory_2024.short: In 2024 the US medicines regulator said no to MDMA therapy for PTSD.
cl_mdma_regulatory_2024.but: We read news and other reports about the decision, not the regulator's own papers.
how: A news report says most of the regulator's expert panel did not think the data showed that the treatment worked.
All but one of those experts said the benefits did not outweigh the risks.
The company says the regulator asked for another large trial.

cl_mdma_retractions_2024.short: In 2024 a journal withdrew three earlier studies from the MDMA therapy research.
cl_mdma_retractions_2024.but: The journal did not say what the rule-breaking was, or how much data it touched.
how: The three studies came from the earlier, smaller trials of the same research programme.
The journal said the authors knew of serious rule-breaking at one study site and did not tell it.
It also said the authors had not fully declared their ties to the sponsor.
Most of the authors who answered the journal disagreed with the withdrawals.

cl_mdma_ptsd_cost.short: Two critics say price and comparison decide if MDMA therapy is good value.
cl_mdma_ptsd_cost.but: The cost studies come from the company or from people with money ties to it.
how: The company's study compared MDMA therapy with the same talking therapy plus a dummy pill.
The critics, who also have money ties to the company, say it should be compared with the treatments people would otherwise get.
At the company's price, the critics' model needs about 8 years before savings cover the cost.
At a much lower price, the critics' model says it could even save money. No independent study was among the papers read.

cl_mdma_therapy_contested.short: Whether MDMA itself helps PTSD, and for how long, is not settled.
cl_mdma_therapy_contested.but: One sponsor ran both trials, and in the one that asked, most people knew their pill.
how: Two trials found PTSD eased more with MDMA and therapy than with a dummy pill and the same therapy.
But in the second trial most people could tell which pill they had, and neither trial reports measuring what they expected.
No trial we read tested MDMA against usual PTSD talking therapy, and the trial reports say nothing after 4 months.
In 2024 the US regulator said no, and a journal withdrew three earlier studies over rule-breaking at one site.
